# reflect

> reflect is an independent, open-source AI coding agent from GrayCodeAI that lives in your terminal: a Go CLI and Bubble Tea TUI that reads and edits code, runs tests, and manages git through natural language, on any machine with a shell. Model routing goes through Relay, a separate, independently released model runtime consumed via its published public API — no sibling checkout is needed to build, test, or run this repo. Status: active development; contributor source builds are the primary path (see README "Status"). Install and quick-start instructions live in [README.md](README.md) — building from source requires Go 1.27.2+. This file is the agent-facing index: verification, repository map, docs, extension points, and boundaries.

## Verification

Run all of these before proposing changes:

- Branch off `main` first (`feat/<desc>`, `fix/<desc>`, `chore/<desc>`); never commit directly to `main` — open a PR and require green CI (AGENTS.md workflow).
- `go test ./...` — unit tests (`make test`). The suite is race-sensitive (session store, multiagent missions); CI runs everything with `-race` (`make test-race`).
- `go vet ./...` (`make vet`).
- gofumpt + goimports formatting: `make fmt` to fix, `make fmt-check` is the CI-safe check.
- `make lint` — golangci-lint (pinned v2.14.0; configured in `.golangci.yml`).
- `reflect verify` — self-verification of local changes before contributing (`reflect verify --fix` attempts fixes); auto-detects the repo's test/verify command via `internal/testrunner`.
- `make ci` — the full local gate: version-check, module-check, fmt-check, vet, boundary guards, lint, race tests, govulncheck, OpenAPI validation. CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) additionally enforces the commit policy, markdownlint, gosec, coverage floors (65% + per-package), the binary size budget, and deadcode/jscpd/fuzz/smoke jobs.

## Repository map

- `cmd/` — Cobra CLI commands and the Bubble Tea TUI (chat view, slash commands, config panels, mission/review/exec commands); `cmd/reflect/main.go` is the binary entry point; `cmd/compat-test` validates `testdata/compatibility-matrix.json`.
- `internal/engine/` — the agent loop: ChatService (the Session's view of the LLM transport), context governor, compaction, vision/multimodal, self-improvement lifecycle (`internal/engine/lifecycle`).
- `internal/multiagent/` — mission orchestration: parallel sub-agents in separate git worktrees, path-reservation ledger, family messaging, handoff, mission graphs.
- `internal/session/` — session persistence (JSONL, WAL), autosave, branch/fork, checkpoints, handover, and lifeboat (working memory captured before context compaction so the active thread survives).
- `internal/hooks/` — lifecycle hooks: hook decisions, HTTP hooks, file watcher, LSP feedback.
- `internal/snapshot/` — session snapshot capture.
- `internal/codegraph/` — repository code graph: embeddings, vector store, repo memory, multiview queries (cgo with a no-cgo stub fallback).
- `internal/storage/` — resolved on-disk storage paths shared across packages.
- `internal/tool/` — the 40+ built-in tools and their safety layer.
- `internal/features/` — feature packages (chat commands, review, skills, eval, workspace, taste, welcome) behind the internal feature registry.
- `internal/permissions/` — user approval system, permission tiers, auto-learning.
- `internal/contracts/` — cross-repo DTO contracts: `types`, `graph`, `agent`, `policy`, `review`, `verify`, `events`, `harness`.
- `internal/config/` settings, budget tracking, agent personas; `internal/token/` token counting and compression; `internal/mcp/` MCP client; `internal/daemon/` + `internal/api/` background HTTP/SSE server and HTTP API.
- `internal/observability/` metrics, logging, tracing; `internal/resilience/` circuit breaker, rate limiting, retries; `internal/context/repomap` AST repo map; `internal/intelligence/` code intelligence.
- Safety and hygiene packages: `internal/pathsafe`, `internal/toolsafety`, `internal/safewrite`, `internal/securitylog`, `internal/crash`; adopted-capability packages: `internal/smartrouting`, `internal/conversationarc`, `internal/relevanceprune`, `internal/replaycache`, `internal/errhint`, `internal/circuitbreaker`, `internal/installtxn`, `internal/testrunner`.
- ~60 more focused packages live under `internal/` (run `ls internal/` for the full list); nothing outside the repo imports them.
- `scripts/` — boundary-guard, workspace, and release scripts behind the Makefile targets. `testdata/` fixtures. `api/openapi.yaml` validated OpenAPI spec. `.github/actions/reflect` bundled CI GitHub Action.

## Extension points

From AGENTS.md; deeper detail in docs/user-guide/ and docs/plugin-development.md.

- Project instructions: on launch, reflect walks from the working directory up to the nearest git root and injects the first match per directory level, priority `AGENTS.md` > `ZERO.md` > `.zero/AGENTS.md` (case-insensitive basename). Read once at session start; ~8 KiB per file, 32 KiB total cap.
- Personal instructions: `~/.reflect/ZERO.md` (Windows: `%AppData%\reflect\ZERO.md`), injected as `## User guidelines` before project rules; project rules take precedence on conflict.
- Specialists (sub-agents): scopes are built-in > user `~/.reflect/specialists/*.md` > project `./.zero/specialists/*.md`; project overrides user overrides built-in on name collision. Managed with `reflect specialist list|show|create|edit|delete|path`.
- Skills: none bundled by default; markdown instruction files sourced from the separate GrayCodeAI/graycode-skills repo and installed on demand via `reflect skills search|install|list|remove`. Installed to `~/.reflect/skills/` (user) or `./.zero/skills/` / `./skills/` (project).
- Hooks: `beforeReview`, `afterReview`, `sessionStart`, `sessionEnd` — managed with `reflect hook add|remove|list` (e.g. `reflect hook add beforeReview --command "lint-check"`).
- MCP servers: `reflect mcp add --name <name> --url <url>`, `reflect mcp remove <name>`, `reflect mcp list`; configuration detail in docs/mcp-servers.md.
- Plugins: `reflect plugin add --name <name> --path <path>`, `reflect plugin remove <name>`, `reflect plugin list`; guide in docs/plugin-development.md.

## Contracts and boundaries

- Relay is a separate published Go module pinned in `go.mod`. Reflect consumes it ONLY through its stable engine facade; this repo builds, tests, and runs with no sibling checkout (`GOWORK=off` is exported in the Makefile; do not create a parent `go.work`).
- Provider protocols, adapters, catalog metadata, credential mappings, and provider contract tests are implemented in Relay's repository first; Reflect changes stay limited to host UX and facade integration.
- Cross-repo contracts live in `internal/contracts/` (vendored from the removed `github.com/GrayCodeAI/eagle` module): `types`, `graph`, `agent`, `policy`, `review`, `verify`, `events`, `harness`. External consumers vendor these DTOs; there is no published contracts module yet.
- For coordinated local Relay changes, create a gitignored `go.local.mod` overlay with an explicit Relay replacement (`make workspace RELAY_DIR=/path/to/relay`), then run `go test -modfile=go.local.mod ./...`. Never commit it; verify the normal `go.mod` graph separately before release.
- Boundary guards run in CI and via `make boundaries`: relay-engine-guard (facade-only Relay imports), relay-client-guard (no production relay/client imports), ecosystem-guard, peer-guard, internal-layers-guard, package-boundaries-guard, feature-boundaries-guard, manifest-guard, and check-replace (no local replace directives in `go.mod`).

## Conventions

- Go 1.27.2+. Release builds are `CGO_ENABLED=0` static binaries for linux/darwin/windows on amd64/arm64 (Makefile `build`/`build-all`).
- Conventional Commits. Signed commits are required. No `Co-authored-by:` trailers — the CI commit policy enforces both.
- VERSION (currently 0.0.1) is the single source of truth. `make version-sync` (scripts/sync-version.py) regenerates package/OpenAPI metadata; `make version-check` rejects stale metadata and runs in `make ci`.
- Tests live next to the source (`foo_test.go` beside `foo.go`), table-driven where practical; the race detector is standard (`make test-race`); golden help fixtures regenerate via `make update-golden`.
- Formatting is gofumpt + goimports (`make fmt`), not plain gofmt.
- Feature branches off `main`; never commit directly; merge only with green CI.
- Host-neutral rule: never import Relay internals directly — engine facade only (enforced by relay-engine-guard).
